text:
maria.g: heads-up: we're seeing a sustained spike of apiserver 502/503s in southamerica region since ~06:12 UTC, correlated with controller-manager reconcile backlog and a nasty GPU attach delay for new pods. noticed a wave of keepalive reuse failures from NAT gateways.
aj: saw alerts. is this the NAT/conntrack issue again or something else?
maria.g: looks different — conntrack counts are fine, but keepalives are getting coalesced by the NAT and then we get a bunch of half-open TCPs. that causes apiserver proxy pool to exhaust file descriptors -> transient 5xx.
omar: any kube-apiserver logs or proxy logs we can paste?
maria.g: paste from api-proxy in the affected AZ: ```time="2026-03-21T06:12:34Z" level=error msg="proxy request failed" err="write tcp 10.2.4.5:6443->10.3.7.88:56712: write: connection reset by peer" count=142```
luke: controller-manager shows long lease reacquire times and a reconcile queue surge, leader-election jitter visible: "failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = Unavailable" repeated.
aj: are GPU attach failures tied to this?
maria.g: yes — new pod scheduling tries to attach GPUs, nodes call back to control plane to mount volumes / update status; with apiserver flakiness the ack windows lengthen and scheduler retries pile up. result: pods stay Pending and GPU capacity appears artificially consumed.
omar: mitigations?
maria.g: did an immediate tweak: reduced keepalive timeout on the proxy pool and bumped apiserver file descriptor soft limit on the proxies. added a temporary 30s extra apiserver replica (no LB because this zone's LB is sticky) which helped lowering observed 5xx rate by ~60%.
luke: pushed a small routing change to avoid the problematic NAT gateway for controlplane traffic from that AZ — traffic now uses fallback nat-2 which has more ephemeral port headroom. monitoring shows request tail latency improved.
aj: cost tradeoff? routing to fallback NAT increases egress costs to the customer but keeps PCCS intact. infra OK with short-term cost.
omar: filing a follow-up to investigate why keepalives were being coalesced; possible kernel tuning regression on the NAT boxes after last OS patch.
maria.g: created incident ticket INC-2026-312 and linked the runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/controlplane-nat-smear. tagging oncall for 24h watch.
luke: scoreboard: apiserver 5xx went from 6/min -> 1.5/min after fixes; controller-manager reconcile queue reduced from 9k -> 800. GPU attach Pending reduced by ~85% in the zone.
aj: nice. next steps: 1) revert NAT node kernel patch in non-prod and run soak, 2) increase ephemeral-port range on NATs, 3) add extra LB capacity and consider session affinity reduction, 4) add a proactive synthetic that storms keepalives to detect smear.
omar: will own #1 and #2. maria, pls post any logs or kernel proc tunables you changed.
maria.g: posted sysctl diffs in the ticket: "net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 -> 0, tcp_fin_timeout  -> 15 -> 5" and proxy pool keepalive from 60s -> 15s.
aj: thanks — please keep the incident channel updated and we can convert to postmortem if root cause is kernel patch. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Alert: incident INC-2026-312 created by maria.g (sev: high)
maria.g: internal note: we considered scaling down non-urgent GPU jobs to free up attachments but decided against immediate kills to avoid latency spikes in user workloads — prefer fix-in-place. follow-up plan in ticket. :spiral_calendar:
aj: good call. ping me if it reappears after kernel rollback.
maria.g: will do. closing this thread, moving discussion to the incident channel for SOC + infra steps. :white_check_mark:
